what.heading: What is a conditional?
paragraphs: An `if` statement runs its indented lines only when a condition is `True`. Add `elif` and `else` to choose between several paths. Python checks them from the top and runs only the first one that's `True`.

points.title: if / elif / else
points.text: Pick one path out of several.

points.title: in and not
points.text: `"Lot" in line` checks whether text appears. `not` flips True and False.

points.title: None
points.text: Python's value for "nothing here". Check it with `is None`.

what.code:
if "Expiry" in line:
    print("Found an expiry line")

example.heading: What it looks like
example.caption: `45 < 0` is False, so Python moves on. `45 < 90` is True, so `status` becomes "Expiring soon" and the `else` is skipped.

demos.label: if / elif / else
demos.note: Each value goes down the list of conditions and stops at the first True one.

demos.label: in and not in
demos.note: in checks whether a piece of text appears inside a string. It works on lists too.

demos.label: not
demos.note: not turns False into True, so the if line reads like plain English.

demos.label: None
demos.note: None means no value at all. is None is the usual way to check for it.

try.prompt: Give each document a status from `days_left`: **"No date"** if it's `None`, **"Expired"** if it's below 0, **"Expiring soon"** if it's below 90, and **"OK"** otherwise. Use `if`, `elif` and `else`, and check for `None` first.
try.starter:
docs = [
    ("Certificate of Quality", 400),
    ("BSE/TSE Declaration", 45),
    ("Cover Letter", None),
    ("Chain of Custody", -3),
]
statuses = []
for doc_type, days_left in docs:
    # decide the status with if / elif / else
    status = "?"
    statuses.append(status)

print(statuses)

checks.hint: Delete the starter line status = "?" (or replace it with your if/elif/else), or every status stays "?".
statuses should have one status per document, so 4. Keep the single statuses.append(status) at the end of the loop.
The Cover Letter's days_left is None, so its status should be "No date". Start with if days_left is None:.
The Chain of Custody has -3 days left, so it's "Expired". Python runs only the first True branch, so check days_left < 0 before days_left < 90.
Close. Check the spelling and capitals of each status: "OK", "Expiring soon", "No date", "Expired".

try.stdout_hint: Your statuses are right, but they aren't printed. Keep print(statuses) at the end.
